chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I seek protection with Allah from a bad neighbor in a residence of stay, whose eyes watch you and whose heart guards you; if he sees you in good, it displeases him, and if he sees you in evil, it pleases him.'

key_terms.إِنْ رَآكَ بِخَيْرٍ سَاءَهُ: If he sees you in good, it displeases him
key_terms.إِنْ رَآكَ بِشَرٍّ سَرَّهُ: If he sees you in evil, it pleases him
key_terms.وَيَرْعَاكَ قَلْبُهُ: And his heart guards/cares for you (with ill-will)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for protection from a bad neighbor in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) identifies the 'evil neighbor' as one whose gaze is fixed on the resident, harboring envy in success and delight in misfortune. This description underscores the spiritual and social harm of such neighbors, emphasizing the importance of choosing righteous companions to protect one's peace and faith. The hadith highlights the significance of neighborly rights in Shia tradition, where the neighbor's character can significantly impact one's spiritual well-being.
